chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who died and one of his inheritors acknowledged a debt for a man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is binding upon him in his share.'
ai.seo_question: Does an heir's acknowledgment of the deceased's debt bind the entire estate or just their own share?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of individual liability in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, distinguishing between the deceased's estate and the heirs' personal assets. It establishes that an heir's voluntary acknowledgment of a debt binds only their specific share, protecting the other heirs from being compelled to pay from their portions unless they consent. This ruling underscores the fairness of treating each heir's portion as a distinct unit for debt settlement.
